title: Flosser does not power on
shortDescription: Dead unit — check outlet, cord, and on/off switch.
fullDescription:
Waterpik WP-660 and WP-672 (Aquarius) are mains-powered. If the unit is unresponsive, verify the outlet works, the cord is fully inserted, and any GFCI outlet is not tripped.

Unit must be on a 120V outlet — international travelers need a voltage converter, not just a plug adapter.

fixSteps.title: Reset GFCI
fixSteps.instruction: Press RESET on the bathroom GFCI outlet.

fixSteps.title: Test outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Plug in another device to verify power.

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm mains supply is 120V for US model.

whenToCallPro: If power is confirmed but the unit remains dead.
videoSearchQuery: Waterpik WP-660 wont turn on fix

faq.q: Does the cordless model use the same diagnostics?
faq.a: No, WP-672 is battery-powered — check charge instead.

title: Weak water stream / pressure loss
shortDescription: Clogged tip, valve, or pump intake causes weak flow.
fullDescription:
A sudden drop in pressure usually indicates a clogged jet tip, mineral buildup in the pump valve, or the reservoir seal not engaging. Run a vinegar descale cycle to clear scale.

Check that the reservoir is seated firmly — a crooked seat stops water flow.

fixSteps.title: Swap tip
fixSteps.instruction: Try a spare jet tip to rule out clog.

fixSteps.title: Vinegar descale
fixSteps.instruction: Fill reservoir with 2 tbsp white vinegar + warm water, run until empty, rinse with fresh water.

fixSteps.title: Reseat reservoir
fixSteps.instruction: Press reservoir firmly onto valve until it clicks.

whenToCallPro: Pressure still weak after descaling — pump may need service.

faq.a: Every 1-3 months depending on water hardness.

title: Jet tip stuck — release button won't eject
shortDescription: Mineral buildup locking the tip collet.
fullDescription:
The colored tip collar can seize from mineral deposits. Pressing the eject button should pop the tip in one action.

Soak the handle upside-down in warm vinegar for 15 minutes to dissolve scale.
symptoms: Eject button does not release tip

fixSteps.title: Vinegar soak
fixSteps.instruction: Immerse handle tip-down in warm vinegar for 15 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Rinse and work
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse, then press eject while gently rocking the tip.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate if needed
fixSteps.instruction: Apply a tiny drop of silicone plumber grease to collet.

whenToCallPro: If tip will not release after soak, replace the handle.

faq.a: Yes, diluted — but vinegar is safer for seals.

title: Water leaking from base during use
fullDescription:
Water pooling under the WP-660 typically comes from the reservoir outlet valve. A stuck or damaged silicone flapper allows backflow.

Remove the reservoir, invert it, and inspect the white flapper valve. Replace if cracked.
symptoms: Reservoir drains fast when not in use

fixSteps.title: Inspect valve
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the reservoir and flip it — look at the black/white valve underneath.

fixSteps.title: Reseat flapper
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the flapper is flat and sealing; straighten if curled.

fixSteps.title: Order replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Waterpik for replacement reservoir if valve is damaged.

whenToCallPro: Leaks inside unit base require replacement unit.

title: WP-672 cordless flosser will not charge
shortDescription: Charging LED dark despite connected cable.
fullDescription:
The WP-672 Cordless Advanced uses a USB-like proprietary charger. If the charge LED stays dark, check the cord seating, the 5V USB power source, and ensure the unit is seated on the charging stand evenly.

Corrosion on magnetic contacts is common — wipe both sides with alcohol.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe magnetic contacts on flosser and base with isopropyl.

fixSteps.title: Seat correctly
fixSteps.instruction: Align flosser on stand until magnet snap engages.

whenToCallPro: If cells are dead (runtime <5 min) — unit replacement often cheaper.

faq.q: Can I use any USB cable?
faq.a: Only the Waterpik magnetic cable works with WP-672.

title: Pump noisy or rattling during use
fullDescription:
A loud clacking noise usually means the pump is running dry or has drawn air. Fill the reservoir fully, tilt the unit to expel air, and run for 15 seconds with the tip pointing into the sink.

Persistent rattling after priming points to diaphragm wear.

fixSteps.title: Prime pump
fixSteps.instruction: Run in a sink for 15 seconds with tip down to expel air.

fixSteps.title: Descale
fixSteps.instruction: Run vinegar cycle if noise persists.

whenToCallPro: Loud rattling after descaling — replace unit.

title: Water leaking from handle base
shortDescription: Worn hose O-ring or cracked handle housing.
fullDescription:
Water escaping where the hose connects to the handle typically means the O-rings have dried out or the threads are damaged. Waterpik sells replacement handles (HHL-660 series).

Do not overtighten — O-rings seal by compression, not torque.

fixSteps.title: Inspect O-rings
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew handle from hose and check both O-rings.

faq.a: Yes — Waterpik doesn't sell them separately, but handle is cheap.

title: Pressure dial has no effect on water flow
shortDescription: Dial disconnected from internal pressure valve.
fullDescription:
If the pressure knob on the WP-660 turns without resistance and water pressure no longer changes, the internal shaft has broken off. Unit typically runs at max pressure regardless.

This requires case opening — most owners replace the unit under warranty.
symptoms: Pressure locked at max or min

fixSteps.title: Confirm symptom
fixSteps.instruction: Try turning dial with power on — no audible change confirms issue.

faq.a: No — dial shaft is in pressurized area.

fullDescription: Pump pulse irregular. Common diagnostic on Waterpik water flosser. Resolve by following manufacturer service procedure.

fixSteps.instruction: Clean charging contacts or ports with soft cloth.

whenToCallPro: If reset/charge doesn't fix, contact warranty service.
